clue.text: I am, by the way, facing tax that's excessive

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a mode is a way or manner of doing something
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: An aside from someone grumbling that the tax they face is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: IM (I'm) then MODE (way) then RATE (tax); 'by the' and 'facing' only join the pieces. 'Rates' were the old British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something going beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: Active nitre to put in the ground

indicators.note: active letters move about and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: Lively saltpetre to be buried in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to place it in a grave.

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: the boulders shelter the cold letter by holding it inside

parts.note: rocks are boulders

explanation.surface: Low boulders give cover to birds out of the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is not short; it is the noise a cow makes, MOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Male red grouse are game birds of upland heath.

clue.text: Absolutely refuse to change the will

definitions.text: Absolutely refuse to change the will

parts.words: Absolutely refuse to change the will
parts.note: reads as refusing to alter a testament, but it means stubbornly resisting any change of mind

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be stubborn and resist persuasion.

clue.text: Wine can be an awful stainer

indicators.note: an awful stainer is jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Red wine spilt on a tablecloth makes a terrible stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be an awful' links; 'awful' rearranges STAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: See punt drifting, and become nervous

indicators.note: letters that drift move out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Watching a punt drift away makes someone anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting tense is the physical sign of anxiety.

indicators.note: to put something around is to turn it about, so the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument, a piece of the brass section

explanation.surface: A list of items: a border, a brass fitting, something placed round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass piece' looks like a metal fitting but is an instrument, TUBA; 'put around' turns it to ABUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To border land is to lie next to it, touching at the boundary.
A brand is an old word for a sword, as is this word; a macaroni was an 18th-century dandy, also called a blade.

indicators.note: the firm word is placed inside the walk word

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means firm, as in a sure footing

explanation.surface: A respected company with offices in a particular street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but is SURE, put inside TREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cherished is valued and held in high regard.

parts.note: theatre words: put on a play of the Restoration era, read as staging a comeback

explanation.definitionFit: To make a comeback is to recover from a setback.

parts.note: 'though' can mean allowing that, granting that

explanation.surface: Setting aside time to meditate.
explanation.definitionFit: Meditation is deep reflection, the act of considering something in the mind.

clue.text: Chemical container turned to face class

indicators.note: turned round, so the word for the container is read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a container
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A chemical drum being rotated so it faces a group of students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses TIN to NIT; 'to face' just puts it beside RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt of nitric acid, used in fertilisers and explosives, is a chemical compound.

clue.text: One cleric prepared to act as a peacemaker

indicators.note: the letters are made ready in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest gets ready to step in and settle a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the nine letters of ONE CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Bringing quarrelling parties back into harmony is what a peacemaker does.

indicators.note: something reported is said aloud, so a word for scratch is matched by its sound

parts.note: a graze is a scratch on the skin

explanation.surface: News that some racehorses have been withdrawn from a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratch' reads as withdrawing a horse from a race, but it is GRAZE, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey horses are commonly called by their colour in the plural.

indicators.note: looking back over something runs the eye the other way, so the officer's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer

explanation.surface: A military officer surveying an American location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking over' reverses COL (colonel) to LOC, then US follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a site or position, a Latin word for spot.

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
a scrape is a predicament, a plight

explanation.surface: Striking a match to get some light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike (scrape)' suggests lighting a match, but it is LAM plus PLIGHT; 'to produce' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow given off by a lamp is a form of illumination.

parts.note: APP is a written abbreviation for approved
a raiser is one who raises, that is builds, a structure

explanation.surface: A valuer arrives with an approved builder.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuer is someone who sets a price on property or goods.

parts.note: looks like real estate, but is the quality of being firm and steady

explanation.definitionFit: Steadiness, the quality of being firm and not easily moved.

clue.text: Runner has trouble on uneven green

parts.note: being in a mess is being in trouble

indicators.note: an uneven green is out of order, so its letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: A golfer or bowler struggling on a bumpy green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uneven' rearranges GREEN into ENGER, which follows MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is someone who carries messages, as in a battlefield runner.
Ulysses S. Grant was a Union army officer of top rank; broad and all-inclusive is a second sense.

indicators.note: upset Tories are knocked over, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Right-wing Conservatives in turmoil, like a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: A donnybrook is a free-for-all brawl, named after an Irish fair near Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: People in a brawl are those causing a violent public disturbance.

parts.note: land is an area of ground

explanation.surface: A creature coming from the eastern region.
explanation.definitionFit: An African antelope, the largest of its kind.

indicators.note: the two lines sit on either side of the president, bordering him

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL
Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

explanation.surface: Lines drawn around a portrait of President Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag marks or identifies something, and to tag is to mark.

clue.text: Pound in money-box-or is it empty?

indicators.note: the pound sign sits inside the money-box word

parts.note: a money-box is a piggy bank
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A coin in the piggy bank, or is the box empty?
explanation.definitionFit: A blank space or page has nothing on it.

clue.text: The inventive kind, in a word

definitions.text: The inventive kind, in a word

parts.words: The inventive kind, in a word
parts.note: 'in a word' looks like 'in short', but it says what is invented: a person who coins new words

explanation.definitionFit: One who coins new vocabulary is inventive with words.

parts.note: twee means sweet or cute in a cloying way

explanation.surface: A sweet little girl dressed in Scottish clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Woollen cloth from the Scottish Borders, worn as jackets and suits.

clue.text: Building site employee increasingly workshy after gallon

indicators.note: the lazy word follows the gallon abbreviation

parts.note: more workshy is lazier

explanation.surface: A builder growing ever more idle after a gallon of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse lists LAZIER first but 'after' puts it behind G.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits window panes works on building sites.

clue.text: One in a cell as before, doing time

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: doing as in 'done over', reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner back inside as before, serving another sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing time' looks like a prisoner, but 'doing' rearranges TIME into MITE after ERE; 'as' is a link. The cell is a monk's or hermit's, not a prison's.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit, especially a religious recluse, lives alone in a small cell.

indicators.note: the word comes from inside the phrase, so its letters are taken from within it

explanation.surface: A man who comes from the attractive village of Kettlewell.
explanation.walkthrough: Kettlewell is a village in Yorkshire, and a tyke is a Yorkshireman, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshireman is called by this nickname.

parts.note: a reflective view sounds thoughtful, but describes eyes like mirrors, dull and staring

explanation.definitionFit: Describes eyes that are dull and expressionless, as from drink or fatigue.
